title: Telemetry stitching roadmap + trace probe manifest
body:
Context / goal:

This note captures a lightweight roadmap and an actionable manifest for stitching metrics, trace anchors, and dashboard widgets across token-serving inference flows. The aim is a cost-aware set of probes and consolidated SLI mappings that support fast RCA for regressions (latency, throughput, cache-warmth, and output-quality proxies).

Constraints and guiding principles:
- Minimize cardinality explosion: prefer derived aggregates and labeled rollups over per-tenant dimensionality unless high QPS.
- Cost-first sampling: prioritize spans for cold-cache and high-variance flows; use probabilistic sampling for steady-state.
- Operator-first dashboards: default view surfaces 3 quick actions (isolate model, rollback, throttle).
- Incremental rollout: 4-week cadence for telemetry changes, with canary on low-traffic models.

Decision matrix (priority -> criteria):
- P0 (investigate quickly): user-facing latency regressions, SLO burn > 30% in 1h, KV cache eviction spikes
- P1 (monitor & improve): token-cost anomalies, tail-CPU/GPU utilization, trace link gaps
- P2 (nice-to-have): per-customer fine-grained panels, long-tail token-distribution histograms

Metric definitions (compact list):
1) inference.request_latency_ms.p50/p95/p99
   owner: eng-serving-runtime
   description: end-to-end time from API ingress to last token emitted (ms)
   query: percentile(latency_ms, [50,95,99]) grouped by model, route
   alert: p95 > 300ms sustained 5m for hosted tier

2) kvcache.warmth_ratio
   owner: eng-serving-runtime
   description: fraction of requests served from KV cache prefix hits
   query: sum(kv_hits)/sum(kv_lookups) by model_version
   alert: drop > 10% vs baseline over 30m

3) batching.batch_size_mean
   owner: platform-engineering
   description: mean batch size used by runtime, useful to correlate cost and latency
   query: avg(batch_size) over 5m
   alert: sudden drop (>=30%) indicates routing/fanout issues

4) token_cost_per_request_usd
   owner: finance-observability
   description: estimated token cost (compute+memory) per request for billing windows
   query: (gpu_token_cost + memory_amortization)/requests
   alert: monthly trend exceeding forecasted budget by 10%

Span and trace conventions (rules to standardize anchors):
- root span: inference.request (tags: request_id, customer_id?, model, route, mode:hosted|dedicated|private)
- child spans: request.validation, routing.policy, kvcache.lookup, batch.wait, model.infer, response.serialize
- tag key conventions: snake_case, short values: model=redwood-7b.q4_0, region=us-west1, route=chat_v2
- correlation ids: always include request_id and session_id; where privacy-sensitive, use hashed customer_id for traces destined to shared dashboards

Sampling plan (operational):
- default: 1% probabilistic sampling across all requests (keeps cost predictable)
- adaptive upsample rules (captured in probe manifest):
  * upsample to 100% for requests that hit: kvcache.miss && latency > p95_baseline
  * upsample to 10% for requests with model.infer time > p95_model
  * deterministic tracing for all error responses (status >= 500) and for canary model versions
- retention tiers: hot traces (upsampled/deterministic) kept 90d, default samples kept 14d

Trace probe manifest (first-cut):
- probe: cold-cache-warmth-sampler
  scope: fanout & multi-tenant routes
  trigger: kvcache.lookup == miss
  sampling: force (100%) for first request of session and 10% for subsequent 5 requests
  why: cold-cache is the highest-likelihood cause of sudden tail latency spikes

- probe: batch-empty-wait-anchor
  scope: dedicated GPU pools where batching policy applies
  trigger: batch.wait > configured_window && batch.size < expected_lower_quantile
  sampling: 100% when triggered
  why: detect pathological routing that prevents batching which hurts throughput

- probe: model-fallback-trace
  scope: routing fallback logic between model variants
  trigger: routing.fallback == true
  sampling: 100% for first 100 events/day per model pair (rate-limited)
  why: understand quality vs latency tradeoffs during fallbacks

Dashboard – operator surface sketch (top row = triage):
- left: SLA tile (p99 latency, error rate, SLO burn) with one-click actions: rollback, throttle, reroute
- middle: heatmap of p95 latency by model_version (y) × route (x), color-coded by delta vs baseline. Hover reveals recent traces link.
- right: cost ticker (token_cost_per_request_usd) and recent budget variance chart (7d, 30d)
- below: probe panel (list of active trace probes with last fired timestamp, link to a representative trace)

Widget design notes (practical):
- heatmap buckets: use relative deltas to baseline, not raw ms — this keeps focus on regressions across models
- hover prefetch: widget should include a trace-link id so operator can open a pre-filtered trace explorer in one click
- guard rails: restrict per-tenant rows to sticky mode only for SREs; default view aggregated per route/model

Rollout plan (4-week sprint cycles):
Week 1: implement metrics and trace tags in staging; add kvcache.warmth_ratio and batch_size instrumentation
Week 2: deploy sampling policy + probe manifests to canary cluster (1% traffic) and verify cost impact
Week 3: dashboard plumbing — heatmap widget + probe list; run tabletop with SREs & solutions ENG
Week 4: promote to prod with a 48h monitoring window; follow with 2-week observation before wide rollouts of per-tenant dimensions

Acceptance criteria (before GA):
- end-to-end trace links from heatmap -> trace explorer open within 3 clicks
- KB: realized sampling cost overhead < 15% on observability bill for the canary cluster
- operator feedback score >= 3/5 from a short usability survey after 1 week

Open questions / risks:
- Do we need per-customer cold-cache tracing for top 10 customers? (privacy + cost tradeoffs)
- How to safely roll out per-tenant widgets in the console without exploding query cost? (options: sampling, cached widgets, async precomputation)
- Are current tag-value cardinalities (model_version tags) already causing metric-series explosion in Prometheus backend? Need inventory check.

Next steps (owner actions):
- Rhea: prototype kvcache.warmth_ratio query and add to staging dashboards (by 2026-02-20)
- Dylan: add span tagging to model.infer and batch.wait spans (PR in obs-instrumentation; target 219)
- Maya: connect heatmap widget to trace explorer link flow and validate hover payload size

Appendix: quick sample queries (Prometheus-like pseudo):
- kv warm ratio: sum(rate(kvcache_hits_total[5m])) by (model_version) / sum(rate(kvcache_lookups_total[5m])) by (model_version)
- p95 latency: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(inference_request_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, model_version, route))

Notes to self: keep this doc living. Expect iterations after tabletop 2026-02-23.
